mintAuthority.summary: Native feUSD issuance is confined to the HyperEVM Liquity-v2-fork CDPs against HYPE, kHYPE, wstHYPE, and bridged BTC at user-set interest rates. Each of the four active branches authorizes its BorrowerOperations and ActivePool contracts to mint feUSD, for eight current token-level minters. The feUSD token (0x02c6a2fa) is an EIP-1967 proxy whose ProxyAdmin (0x44a600c0) is owned by a central admin proxy (0xf42fdd95). That admin proxy's own ProxyAdmin (0xdf1293b4) is owned by a Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 multisig (0x699090e7, 3-of-6, no modules, no guard). HyperCore FEUSD is a noncanonical linked representation assessed separately in Bridge Risk; no HyperCore minter is included here.

controls.label: Felix WHYPE BorrowerOperations
controls.capDescription: User debt issuance is constrained by WHYPE collateral requirements and the branch maxDebtCap; the Felix admin can raise that cap.
controls.evidence: At HyperEVM block 37553335: feUSD token (0x02c6a2fa58cc01a18b8d9e00ea48d65e4df26c70) is an EIP-1967 proxy (implementation slot = 0x444322c3c54908fa5a7842a4f3ff085ec67f2598, proxy admin slot = 0x44a600c031dbdf652500f4a6d84b168056f13692). ProxyAdmin confirmed by getProxyImplementation returning the implementation address. At block 40636026, CollateralRegistry reported exactly four active collaterals; the WHYPE registry resolved this BorrowerOperations address and feUSD borrowerOperationsAddresses(address) returned true.

controls.label: Felix WHYPE ActivePool
controls.capDescription: Mints only accounted WHYPE-branch aggregate interest and batch-management fees derived from branch debt; it has no independent arbitrary-mint entry point.
controls.evidence: At block 40636026, the WHYPE registry resolved this ActivePool address and feUSD activePoolAddresses(address) returned true. The current ActivePool source mints only accounted aggregate interest, Stability Pool yield, and batch-management fees.

controls.label: Felix admin multisig (ultimate upgrade and parameter authority)
controls.evidence: Latest HyperEVM getOwners() on Safe 0x699090e73c4077ef2af42773b31788c6564f079c returned 6 owners, threshold 3, no modules, no guard. This refresh replaces the prior stale owner snapshot that also contained a malformed 39-hex address.

review.evidence: On-chain reads traced the full Felix admin chain: feUSD token (0x02c6a2fa) → ProxyAdmin (0x44a600c0, owner=0xf42fdd95) → nested admin proxy 0xf42fdd95 (implementation 0xd2fe30df..., ProxyAdmin 0xdf1293b4) → 0xdf1293b4 owner()=0x699090e7 → Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 (3-of-6, 6 current EOA signers, no modules, no guard, fallback handler=0x017062a1). Rechecked at HyperEVM block 40435040; the proxy, implementation, and ownership chain is unchanged. The same 0xf42f proxy owns the Felix AddressesRegistry (0x9de1e57049c475736289cb006212f3e1dce4711b). The 3-of-6 Safe is the ultimate admin authority. At block 40636026, CollateralRegistry totalCollaterals() returned 4 and indices 0-3 resolved WHYPE, UBTC, kHYPE, and wstHYPE while index 4 reverted. Each branch registry resolved one BorrowerOperations and one ActivePool address, and all eight corresponding feUSD authorization mappings returned true. Re-verified at HyperEVM block 40980730 (2026-07-20): Safe 0x699090E73c4077eF2aF42773b31788C6564F079c still returns getThreshold()=3 over six owners, getModulesPaginated returned an empty module array, the Safe guard storage slot (0x4a20…34c8) reads zero, and the singleton slot resolves the Safe 1.3.0 masterCopy 0xfb1bffc9d739b8d520daf37df666da4c687191ea. Because that same self-controlled 3-of-6 Safe can raise each branch maxDebtCap and upgrade the feUSD token implementation with no timelock and no independent bound, the branch caps are economically unbounded rather than raiseable. Collateral is held in on-chain branch pools and is continuously readable, so there is no off-chain supply-versus-reserve attestation cadence, and no financial regulator supervises Felix. HyperCore FEUSD is the noncanonical Hyperliquid representation linked to the HyperEVM token; no HyperCore issuer minter is inferred, and its system asset-linkage controls remain an unresolved Bridge Risk evidence gap.
